solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: As London club, wanting a liberal in charge

indicators.note: wanting here means lacking, so the named letters are missing from the club

parts.note: Arsenal is a London football club
A plus L, the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: Someone compares a London football club to one that has lost its Liberal manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a little link word at the start, but it is the definition: As is the chemical symbol of this element. ARSENAL is a London football club; take away A and L to leave ARSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol for the poisonous element arsenic in the periodic table.

clue.text: Dry shirt messed up attending houses

indicators.note: houses means holds inside, so the two letters enclose the rest

parts.note: at means attending, as in 'at a meeting'

indicators.note: messed up signals the letters of shirt are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wet shirt, crumpled, needs drying, while someone attends to housework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' is a verb here: the two-letter word for attending holds the jumbled shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Athirst is an old word for thirsty, so parched or dry.

clue.text: Get brown paper bag without good article

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: without means the good letter is left out of the bag

parts.note: the word as written
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone buys a brown paper bag missing an item.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper. 'brown' belongs to the definition, not to the paper bag.
explanation.definitionFit: To sunbathe is to lie in the sun to get a tan, turning the skin darker.

clue.text: Comfortable spot according to Otto I in north-east

indicators.note: in means the German pronoun sits inside the compass letters

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east
ich is German for I, and Otto stands for a German speaker

explanation.surface: A German named Otto describes his cosy corner in the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: Otto is a typical German name, so 'I according to Otto' is ICH, the German for I.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a position that suits someone well, a comfortable or fitting place.

clue.text: Firm understood to dismiss leader involved in crime

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: to dismiss its leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: implicit means understood without being stated

explanation.surface: A company is believed to have sacked its boss over a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' here means the first letter of the word for understood, not a company boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Being complicit means sharing in wrongdoing as an accomplice or participant.

clue.text: Underground drain hasn't rain around entry

indicators.note: around signals turning the combined letters the other way round

parts.note: the Tube is London's Underground railway

indicators.note: hasn't means the word drain is without the letters of rain

parts.note: the word as written, before the removal

explanation.surface: A sewer in a dry spell lets nothing flow round its inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground railway; 'Underground drain' reads as one sewer, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A debut is a first appearance, someone's entry onto a stage or into public life.

clue.text: Strip of rank ham after days

indicators.note: after means the ham comes later than the days in the answer

parts.note: to ham is to overact, to emote

explanation.surface: An officer loses a stripe after days of eating ham.
explanation.walkthrough: A ham is an over-the-top actor, and to emote is to act with exaggerated feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To demote is to lower someone's rank, which is to strip them of a higher one.

clue.text: Where workers may be seen in High Barnet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hive where worker bees live
second meaning: a tall bouffant hairstyle; barnet is rhyming slang for hair

explanation.walkthrough: High Barnet is a real London Tube station, which disguises the second sense: barnet (Barnet Fair) is Cockney slang for hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The hive is a home for worker bees, and the 1960s piled-up hairdo is named after its shape.

clue.text: Student of French you support on course

parts.note: tu is the familiar French for you
a tee supports the ball on a golf course

explanation.surface: A student of French is backed during the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a study course, but it is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutee is a pupil taught by a tutor.

clue.text: Figure Homer represented eating butter up

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the reversed butter goes inside
represented signals the letters of Homer are rearranged
up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a pat is a small portion of butter

explanation.surface: A poet's work features an image of butter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads a word from bottom to top; a pat is a small block of butter.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphor is a figure of speech, an image that calls one thing by another's name.

clue.text: Man in Macbeth, say, moving east

indicators.note: moving means the east letter is shifted to a different spot in the word

parts.note: Macbeth was Thane of Glamis and Cawdor, an example of a thane
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A character in Macbeth is described as heading eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: THANE, a Scottish noble title Macbeth held, has its final E brought to the front to give ETHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethan is a male first name, so a man is called this; names as definitions are a crossword staple.

clue.text: Perhaps arm cracking whip in some French dairy

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a cat, as in cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
an arm is an example of a limb, or member

explanation.surface: Someone cracks a whip with their arm inside a French dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the arm as just one example of a limb; cat-o'-nine-tails explains the whip.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft cheese from Normandy, so it is one example of French dairy produce.

clue.text: A prison bordering on a quantity of land

indicators.note: bordering means the prison surrounds the next piece on both sides

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement, a prison
RE means on or about, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A jail sits next to a piece of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' meaning concerning is a Latin-derived usage from business letters ('re your enquiry').
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is an area measured in acres, so a quantity of land.

clue.text: Web article in French about Greek

indicators.note: about means going round, so the article wraps the Greek word

parts.note: le is a French definite article
Attic is the Greek dialect of Athens, and Attica its region

explanation.surface: A web page offers a French article on a Greek topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Web' suggests the internet, but it means a criss-cross structure; Attic is the dialect and culture of ancient Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a criss-cross framework of strips, like a web of interlaced lines.

clue.text: Retire from hospital? Dismissal following appeal

indicators.note: following means the dismissal comes after the appeal in the answer

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
it means sex appeal, as in having 'it'
being fired is getting the sack

explanation.surface: A worker is retired from a hospital, sacked after losing an appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retire' here means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: Hit the sack is an informal idiom for going to bed, and to retire also means going to bed at night.

clue.text: Climbing mountains, call to spare no expense

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Alps are mountains
a shout is a call

explanation.surface: Mountaineers yell a call while climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash out is an idiom meaning to spend freely or lavishly.

clue.text: Expert leaves saying part of speech

indicators.note: leaves means the expert departs from the saying

parts.note: a proverb is a traditional saying
a pro is an expert or professional

explanation.surface: An expert walks out, offering a remark about grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: PROVERB loses PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb is one of the grammatical word classes, the doing word of a sentence.

clue.text: British troops accordingly keeping queen's men in order

parts.note: the RE, Royal Engineers, are British troops

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the queen goes in

parts.note: then means accordingly, as a result
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen, as on a monarch's cipher

explanation.surface: British soldiers guard the queen's men and keep them in line.
explanation.walkthrough: The RE (Royal Engineers) is a British army corps. 'order' suggests discipline, but it is a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Brethren are the brothers of a religious order or fellowship, so its men.

clue.text: Group of mates round after lager is drunk

indicators.note: after means the round comes later than the anagram
drunk signals the letters are tipsily rearranged

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A group of friends buys a round after drinking lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mates' suggests pals at the pub, but it means sexual partners, the women of a harem.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is a harem, the wives and concubines of a sultan, hence a group of mates.

clue.text: Something that is so out of time in religious book

indicators.note: out of means the time letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: a truth is something that is so, a fact

explanation.surface: A fact is found to be out of date in a holy text.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUTH loses one T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a book of the Old Testament in the Bible, named after its heroine.

clue.text: By losing energy, where poor driver may end up

indicators.note: losing means the energy letter is taken out

parts.words: where poor driver may end up
parts.note: a bad golf drive lands in the rough
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A bad motorist runs out of fuel and ends up stranded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist, but it is a golfer hitting a drive into THE ROUGH, the long grass off the fairway.
explanation.definitionFit: Through and by both mean by means of, as in 'through hard work'.

clue.text: Reasonable skirts silver and trendy

indicators.note: skirts means goes around the edges, so the first phrase surrounds the metal

parts.note: all there means mentally sound, reasonable
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Sensible skirts with silver trim are fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' looks like clothing, but it is the containment verb: ALL THERE goes around AG.
explanation.definitionFit: All the rage is an idiom for very fashionable or popular at the moment.

clue.text: Believer in a philosophical idea and its main ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed, as in a mill, so the letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A philosopher believes an idea and its central basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main ground' reads like 'main basis', but 'ground' is the anagram signal for ITS MAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An animist holds the belief that natural things, like trees and rivers, have souls.

clue.text: Waste the money one's paid in the Home Counties?

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in south-east England, SE
a wage is the money one is paid

explanation.surface: A commuter complains that pay in the London area is squandered.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, all in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewage is waste matter carried away in sewers.

clue.text: Extraction tool appropriate to mushrooms

parts.note: for, as in 'a job for him', means suited or appropriate to
ceps are edible porcini mushrooms

explanation.surface: A tool for gathering is recommended for picking mushrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceps are pincers used, for example, by dentists and surgeons to pull things out.

clue.text: Lifted picture from big book

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means raised, read upwards

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting
of means from, as in 'a man of Kent'

explanation.surface: A picture has been cut out of a large book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' suggests stolen, but it turns OIL OF upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a large book made of sheets folded once, the biggest standard size.

clue.text: Rotten king: terrible ruler going over outline of speech

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: going over means turning over, so the ruler's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ivan the Terrible was the Russian tsar

indicators.note: the outline of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A rotten king and a terrible ruler rehearse a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivan the Terrible was a 16th-century Russian tsar; IVAN reversed is NAVI, and the outer letters of 'speech' give SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Knavish means dishonest or roguish, like a knave, which is close to calling someone rotten.

clue.text: Boat unaffected after capsizing?

indicators.note: unaffected after capsizing means the word is the same turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: the boat itself, whose letters read the same both ways

explanation.surface: A boat comes through a capsize undamaged.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same in both directions, so turning it over changes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A kayak is a small, narrow canoe paddled with a double-bladed oar.

clue.text: Praising person famous for driving on the right

parts.note: Niki Lauda was a Formula One world champion driver
the Tories are the right-wing party in British politics

explanation.surface: A famous driver gets praise for keeping to the right side of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Niki Lauda, the Austrian racing driver, gives LAUDA; a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudatory means expressing praise, from the Latin laus, a word for commendation.

clue.text: Folk knowledge about India is current in Europe

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the knowledge wraps the letter

parts.note: lore is traditional folk knowledge
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Traditional knowledge about India is now fashionable in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'fashionable now', but it means a flow of water, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, and a river is a current of flowing water.

clue.text: Taps into valuable material to make pigment

indicators.note: into means the taps go inside the material

parts.note: ore is rock mined for its valuable metal
taps are marked C and H, for cold and hot

explanation.surface: Someone taps into a rich seam to produce a colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Taps are labelled C (cold) and H (hot); those letters go inside ORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy clay pigment, yellow to brown, used by painters since prehistory.

clue.text: Surveillance operation ditching Sierra or Escort

indicators.note: ditching means dropping, so the letter is removed from the operation

parts.note: a stakeout is police surveillance of a place
S is Sierra in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Police watch two models of Ford car, the Sierra or the Escort.
explanation.walkthrough: Sierra and Escort were both Ford cars, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone out is to escort them on a date or outing.
